_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Philippines covering pre-colonial barangays, Magellan's arrival 1521, Spanish colonization (1565-1898, Galleon Trade, Catholicism), Katipunan revolution, Philippine-American War 1899-1902, US colonial period, WWII Japanese occupation, independence 1946, Marcos dictatorship 1972-1986, People Power Revolution (EDSA), Moro insurgency, Duterte's drug war, and democratic volatility.

religion.note: Only Christian-majority country in Asia (Spanish legacy); Catholic Church politically powerful; Mindanao and Sulu Archipelago Muslim (Moro); Iglesia ni Cristo (1914, Filipino church); animism persists in highlands

ethnic_groups.name: Tagalog
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest group; Metro Manila and surrounding; Tagalog basis of Filipino; culturally dominant; Central Luzon

ethnic_groups.name: Bisaya/Visayan (Cebuano, Hiligaynon, Waray)
ethnic_groups.notes: Cebuano (Cebu, Mindanao) largest single Visayan group (~21%); Visayas islands; distinct languages; some Bisaya resent Tagalog linguistic dominance

ethnic_groups.name: Ilocano
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern Luzon; industrious farmers; significant diaspora; Marcos family is Ilocano

ethnic_groups.name: Moro (Tausug, Maguindanao, Maranao, etc.)
ethnic_groups.notes: Muslim Filipinos; Mindanao/Sulu/Palawan; Bangsamoro Autonomous Region; MILF/MNLF insurgencies; sultanates (Sulu, Maguindanao); centuries-long resistance to Christian colonization

ethnic_groups.name: Indigenous (Igorot, Lumad, Mangyan, etc.)
ethnic_groups.notes: Upland minorities; animist; Cordillera (Igorot/Ifugao rice terraces UNESCO); Lumad (Mindanao); Aeta/Negrito (oldest inhabitants); marginalized

ethnic_groups.name: Chinese Filipino (Tsinoy)
ethnic_groups.notes: Dominant in business; mestizo elite; Hokkien dialect; 'taipans'; intermarriage common; colonial-era traders

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Spanish mestizo, American, Japanese, Korean)
ethnic_groups.notes: Approximate; Spanish/American colonial legacy; Korean expatriates growing; mixed-race common

country_profile.notes_unique: Only Christian-majority Asian country; 7,641 islands; Magellan killed in Mactan 1521 by Lapu-Lapu; Bataan Death March (WWII); People Power Revolution 1986 (ousted Marcos); Jeepneys; OFWs (Overseas Filipino Workers, ~10% population, remittances 10% GDP); Mount Pinatubo 1991 eruption; Typhoon Haiyan 2013; Duterte's drug war (~30,000 killed 2016-22); Marcos Jr elected 2022 (son of dictator)

trade.notes: Electronics/semiconductors 50%+ of exports; BPO services massive; banana/coconut major agri-exports; trade deficit offset by remittances/BPO; PEZA economic zones.

infrastructure.notes: Build Build Build infrastructure program; Manila MRT/LRT systems; NAIA airport notorious congestion (New Manila International Airport planned); inter-island shipping critical.

governance_indices.notes: Marcos Jr. presidency (2022); dynastic politics; drug war legacy (Duterte); Rappler/press freedom concerns; Bangsamoro autonomous government; active civil society.

country_profile.national_motto: For God, People, Nature, and Country (Maka-Diyos, Maka-Tao, Makakalikasan at Makabansa)

geography.terrain: Archipelago of 7,641 islands; mountainous volcanic terrain; narrow coastal lowlands; tropical forests
geography.notes: 7,641 islands; Ring of Fire location; world's 5th longest coastline; typhoon corridor (20+/year); Tubbataha Reef UNESCO; Palawan underground river; Benham Rise.

economy_extended.notes: BPO/outsourcing powerhouse (#1 globally for voice); OFW remittances vital; demographic dividend opportunity; infrastructure program 'Build Build Build'; inequality persistent.

health.notes: Universal Health Care Act (2019); nurse/doctor brain drain to Gulf/West; Dengvaxia controversy impacted vaccination; highest TB burden in Western Pacific; PhilHealth reforms.

food_agriculture.notes: World's largest coconut producer; major banana/pineapple exporter; rice import-dependent; 70%+ farmers landless; typhoons regularly destroy harvests; CARP agrarian reform legacy.

security_stability.internal_conflicts: NPA communist insurgency (winding down); Abu Sayyaf/IS-Philippines
security_stability.border_disputes: South China Sea (Spratly Islands, Scarborough Shoal) vs. China
security_stability.notes: South China Sea frontline state; Marawi siege (2017); Bangsamoro Autonomous Region peace process; NPA insurgency longest in Asia; EDCA bases expanded (US); China tensions.

environment_climate.notes: World's most disaster-prone country (typhoons, earthquakes, volcanoes); Super Typhoon Haiyan (2013); Taal volcano; coral triangle biodiversity; plastic pollution major issue.

demographics_extended.notes: World's 13th most populous (115M+); OFW (10M+ abroad) backbone of economy; young demographic dividend; 180+ languages; Tagalog/Filipino lingua franca; Catholic 80%+.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: Archipelago of 7,641 islands; BPO powerhouse; largest Catholic nation in Asia; major diaspora.

world_heritage_sites: Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: Philippine Inquirer, Philippine Star (English); Manila Bulletin; ABS-CBN, GMA; active social media (top globally in usage time).
cultural_heritage.notes: 300+ years Spanish colonialism; American period (1898–1946); People Power Revolution (1986); Catholicism 90%+; BPO capital; Christmas starts September.

energy.notes: World's second-largest geothermal energy producer; Malampaya gas field (declining); coal imports growing; Bataan Nuclear Power Plant (never operated); renewable energy act (2008).

human_rights_gender.lgbtq_legal_status: Legal but no anti-discrimination law; SOGIE bill pending
human_rights_gender.notes: Duterte drug war (2016–2022, thousands killed, ICC investigation); EJKs; Marcos family return; red-tagging of activists; strong women's rights record.

legal_system.legal_tradition: Mixed: civil law (Spanish), common law (American), Islamic law (BARMM)
legal_system.sharia_applicability: Sharia in BARMM (Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao)
legal_system.customary_law_role: Indigenous Peoples' Rights Act (IPRA, 1997) recognises customary law
legal_system.icc_membership: Withdrew (2019, effective); ICC retains jurisdiction for pre-withdrawal acts
legal_system.notes: Supreme Court (15 justices); writ of amparo/habeas data (human rights writs); BARMM Bangsamoro Organic Law (2019); Cybercrime Prevention Act.

tourism.notes: 'It's More Fun in the Philippines' branding; island tourism; diving; Boracay rehabilitation (2018); medical/wellness tourism growing.

transport.notes: Jeepney (iconic transport); Manila traffic among world's worst; North-South Commuter Railway (under construction); inter-island ferries essential; PAL, Cebu Pacific main airlines.

current_leader.name: Bongbong Marcos (Ferdinand Marcos Jr.)
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Son of dictator Ferdinand Marcos; won landslide; Sara Duterte VP; historical revisionism concerns; social media campaign; Imelda Marcos (mother) still alive

former_leaders.name: Rodrigo Duterte
former_leaders.notes: Populist; Davao City mayor; 'War on Drugs' (~30,000 extrajudicial killings); ICC investigation; China pivot; vulgar rhetoric; 70%+ approval; daughter Sara is current VP

former_leaders.name: Benigno Aquino III (Noynoy)
former_leaders.notes: Son of Corazon Aquino and Ninoy Aquino; anti-corruption; economic growth; Typhoon Haiyan 2013; died 2021

former_leaders.name: Gloria Macapagal Arroyo
former_leaders.notes: Economist; succeeded Estrada; election fraud allegations (Hello Garci scandal); corruption charges (later acquitted); daughter of President Diosdado Macapagal

former_leaders.name: Joseph Estrada
former_leaders.notes: Actor; populist; EDSA II uprising removed him (corruption); convicted then pardoned; later Manila mayor

former_leaders.name: Fidel V. Ramos
former_leaders.notes: General; economic liberalization; peace talks with MNLF; Protestant (unusual)

former_leaders.name: Corazon Aquino
former_leaders.notes: Widow of Ninoy Aquino; People Power Revolution; restored democracy; 7 coup attempts; 'Mother of Democracy'; died 2009

former_leaders.name: Ferdinand Marcos
former_leaders.notes: Martial Law 1972-81; dictatorship; crony capitalism; $10B embezzled; wife Imelda (3,000 shoes); EDSA Revolution ousted; exiled to Hawaii; died 1989; National Hero burial 2016 under Duterte

former_leaders.name: Diosdado Macapagal
former_leaders.notes: Father of Gloria Arroyo; Independence Day moved to June 12 (from July 4)

former_leaders.name: Manuel Roxas
former_leaders.notes: First president of independent Philippines; post-WWII reconstruction; died in office

former_leaders.name: José Rizal
former_leaders.notes: National hero (not president); executed 1896 by Spanish; Noli Me Tángere/El Filibusterismo; martyr
